title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference | Week 2 vs. Seattle Seahawks
headline: Right guard is an open competition between Isaiah Adams (back at practice after a rolled ankle) and Jon Gaines. Ari lost a key defender to IR for at least four weeks, and Max Melton is limited.
summary: LaFleur said a player (named "Keaton" in the captions, not clearly identifiable on the roster) is on IR for at least four weeks, and the team will reevaluate after that. Max Melton left late in the game, will be limited, and the coach expects him to be okay. Isaiah Adams returns to practice after getting rolled up on in practice, and the coach praised his camp. He also praised Jon Gaines and would not say who starts at right guard on Sunday, saying only that the team wants whoever gives the best chance to move the ball. Offensively, LaFleur felt the unit was slow and sluggish getting in and out of the huddle, left a lot on the field in the run game, and was 0-for-1 in the red zone, though he defended the end-of-half drive. He praised Jacoby Brissett for saving a play against edge pressure. On defense he singled out Mack Wilson's physical, decisive play. He called Simi Fehoko's special teams honor deserved. Seattle is the opponent, with Drew Lock starting over Sam Darnold, and LaFleur called the Seahawks defense one of the best the league has ever seen. A healthy-scratch question was answered as a "numbers game."

injuries.detail: Missed the final 4-5 minutes of the game; will be limited in practice but the coach expects him to be okay.
Got rolled up on in practice; feeling good and will practice Wednesday, with day-to-day reevaluation.
No injury noted; he is competing at right guard.

signals.claim: Adams is in a competition with Jon Gaines for the starting right guard spot against Seattle.
signals.note: A rolled ankle makes his Sunday status uncertain; the OL matchup affects the run game and pass protection.

signals.claim: Gaines may keep the right guard job on Sunday.
signals.note: Strong play so far puts him in the running to start while Adams is working back.
signals.quote: Gaines has done some really good stuff.

signals.claim: Wilson will remain a key, physical defender in the front seven.
signals.note: His growing trust in his keys makes him a rising IDP option.
signals.quote: he's just playing underneath himself more and more every single time

signals.claim: Melton will be limited in practice this week.
signals.note: The coach expects him to be fine, but monitor his practice reports for IDP purposes.
signals.quote: He'll be limited on there. But he'll be okay.

signals.claim: Brissett remains the starter and made a key play against edge pressure.
signals.note: The coach publicly praised him for saving a red-zone play.
signals.quote: for Jacoby to save us when we got edge off our right side was awesome.

topics.detail: LaFleur said the offense was slow in the huddle and left plays on the field, especially in the run game and red zone, and said the fixes start with coaches.
He called Seattle's defense possibly one of the best the league has seen, noting the team has played them multiple times since late last year.
Drew Lock fills in for Sam Darnold; LaFleur called him efficient, experienced, and unfazed by the moment.
A player the transcript calls Keaton is on IR for at least four weeks; the coach didn't name a replacement. A numbers game decided who was inactive.
Simi Fehoko earned NFC special teams player honors after a key block.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 2 Media Availability | Wednesday, September 16th | Press Conference
headline: Falcons QB Week 2 is unresolved: Penix and Rush practice Wednesday, Tua sits, Strand isn't ruled out, and Bijan's 29-touch Week 1 load isn't a given every week.
summary: Stefanski opened by praising Carolina, the reigning division champs, for a strong QB, multiple outside receivers, a tough run game, a big front (Phillips on the edge) and a good secondary. He said Atlanta will have a quarterback Sunday but has not chosen one, and he repeatedly said he is not ruling anyone out. Tua, whom the transcript renders as 'two', will not practice Wednesday but is improving. Michael Penix Jr. is cleared to practice and progressing, and Cooper Rush will practice fully despite ongoing back treatment. Jack Strand also isn't ruled out. Stefanski called the decision 'day to day', said the game plan has to stay flexible, and would not say who is working with the ones. He was pleased with Rush's development and expects him to improve with more reps, and he attributed the many short throws last week to Carolina's rush and coverage. On Bijan Robinson, he doubted a 29-touch workload would repeat every game and said spreading the ball around helps the offense and Bijan.

injuries.detail: Will not practice Wednesday but is 'getting better'; not ruled out for Sunday. The transcript says 'two', read here as Tua.
Cleared to practice and progressing; Stefanski would not rule him out for Sunday or give a timeline. Rep plan not disclosed.
Still getting treatment on his back but will be a full participant Wednesday; Stefanski wouldn't call him 100%.
Not ruled out for Sunday; Stefanski wouldn't say whether developmental concerns are a factor.

signals.claim: Rush is a candidate to start Sunday and will be a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
signals.note: He is the fallback starter if Penix and Tua can't go, but he played poorly Week 1 and the decision is open.
signals.quote: Very, very pleased with where Cooper is developmentally.

signals.claim: Penix could return as the starter this weekend depending on how Wednesday and Thursday practices go.
signals.note: His return would reset the QB room and the offense, but Stefanski gave no commitment or timeline.
signals.quote: Cleared to practice. Just like all the guys.

signals.claim: Tua misses Wednesday's practice but is improving and is not ruled out for Sunday.
signals.note: Missing practice lowers the odds he starts, but the QB decision remains open.
signals.quote: he's getting better

signals.claim: Strand is still in consideration to play Sunday.
signals.note: He is a long-shot option, but the QB position is wide open.
signals.quote: Jack is not being ruled out for this game.

signals.claim: Bijan is unlikely to repeat 29 touches every game, as the offense plans to spread the ball around more.
signals.note: Expect a possible dip from the Week 1 workload, though he remains the focal point.
signals.quote: while it may take away from those 29 touches in week one

topics.detail: Stefanski called the Panthers sound, with a QB who can make every throw, multiple dangerous outside receivers, a tough run attack, a big powerful front with Phillips rushing the edge, and a good secondary and special teams.
Stefanski stressed flexibility and day-to-day decisions. He acknowledged that a late QB choice complicates game planning, but said teams adapt, and he noted a Thursday night game follows Sunday.

He said the offense didn't play well enough to win. 17 of 22 Rush passes came within five yards of the line, which he attributed to Carolina's pass rush, coverages and batted balls rather than a deliberate plan.
He addressed Olamide Zaccheaus as the emergency QB, saying no team wants to get to that part of the call sheet.
Stefanski praised Za'Darius Smith's energy and authentic leadership as an example of the player-led culture he wants.

title: Jesse Minter Shares Injury Updates on Ja'Kobi Lane, Zay Flowers, T.J. Tampa
headline: Ja'Kobi Lane goes on IR after successful surgery (4-week minimum likely), Zay Flowers and Nnamdi Madubuike are day-to-day, and Chris Moore is promoted to the 53-man roster ahead of the home opener vs. the Saints.
summary: Minter opened by saying Ja'Kobi Lane will be placed on IR after a successful surgery that morning, with a good chance of returning fairly quickly. He said the team is aiming for the minimum IR stay, and Lane will try to shave a week or two off it. Chris Moore is being promoted to the 53-man roster after earning it in Week 1 with his play and special teams versatility. Zay Flowers and Nnamdi Madubuike were both labeled day-to-day, with Flowers described as in a good place but still day-to-day. On T.J. Tampa, Minter said it will probably take some time and the team is still figuring out the best course of action. He urged the receivers to step up, saying the ball can go anywhere in the offense, and he expressed confidence in the offensive coordinator's plan for the available weapons. He praised the Saints offense under Kellen Moore, citing Olave, a second-year quarterback, good backs and tempo. He also said veterans like Trey Hendrickson may get rest days based on how they feel, and that the team is happy with Tyler (the kicker) while keeping Jake Moody on the practice squad.

injuries.detail: Had successful surgery Wednesday morning; will be placed on IR. Team is targeting the minimum IR stay (about four weeks), and he may try to return a week or two sooner.
Described as day-to-day; Minter said he is in a really good place but will be day-to-day.
In the day-to-day category; will be evaluated at the end of the week.
Not at practice; Minter said veteran rest days depend on how players feel coming out of the game, not a specific injury.

signals.claim: Will miss at least the minimum IR stay (about four weeks) before returning.
signals.note: Lane is out for several weeks, removing a receiver option from the Baltimore passing game.
signals.quote: we'll end up putting him on IR. Had a successful surgery this morning.

signals.claim: Flowers' availability for the Saints game will be determined day to day this week.
signals.note: Flowers is the top receiver, so his status heavily affects the passing game and the Ravens' other pass catchers.
signals.quote: Day to day, day to day.

signals.claim: Will be added to the 53-man roster and can contribute at receiver and on special teams.
signals.note: He's in line for added snaps at receiver given the injuries, though still a deep-league option at best.
signals.quote: Chris certainly did that week one.

signals.claim: Madubuike's status will be assessed at the end of the week.
signals.note: Relevant to IDP managers and to the strength of the Ravens' defensive line.
signals.quote: he's in that day to day category as well.

topics.detail: Minter respects Kellen Moore's offense: multiple looks, lots of tempo, a second-year quarterback, Olave as an elite receiver, and good backs and line. New Orleans came back late in Week 1 and forced overtime.
Minter stressed defending home field and feeding off the crowd, especially on defensive third downs and in the red zone. He wants a better start defensively after a poor opening drive in Week 1.
Minter has confidence in Tyler after Week 1 and noted Jake Moody is on the practice squad, saying they'll see how things shake out.
Rest days for veterans like Trey Hendrickson will be decided week to week based on how players feel.
Minter said the offensive coordinator will build a plan around available weapons and told receivers the ball can go anywhere in the offense.

title: Dave Canales:  'We're focused on consistency heading into Atlanta'
headline: Jalen Coker (limited Wednesday) is expected to play Sunday at Atlanta, John Metchie III steps into a bigger WR role after Jimmy Horn Jr. was waived, and Tetairoa McMillan remains the focal point of the pass game.
summary: Canales said Wednesday's practice was about fundamentals and consistency ahead of the trip to Atlanta. Jalen Coker did some team work after an extended warm-up and treatment. The plan is to ramp him up Thursday and fully clear him Friday, and Canales expects him to play. John Metchie III took many of Coker's reps and is trusted by Bryce Young. He is also stepping into return duty after Jimmy Horn Jr. was waived, a move Canales said was driven by the roster spot, with the hope of getting Horn back on the practice squad. Canales said the pass game runs through Tetairoa McMillan, who is moved around to create matchups, and that Xavier Legette had a fantastic practice and is in the game plan. He wants Bryce Young to build on last week's strong game, and said the opponent or stadium doesn't matter. On Atlanta, he expects Kevin Stefanski's system to hold regardless of the QB (Tua Tagovailoa, Michael Penix or Cooper Rush), and he praised Jeff Ulbrich's aggressive, disguise-heavy defense. He called Bijan Robinson (30 touches last week) a multi-faceted threat who needs a disciplined team-tackling plan.

injuries.detail: Did a little in team drills after an extended warm-up and treatment. The plan is to ramp up Thursday and fully clear him Friday. Canales expects him to play Sunday.
Called the team's returner but 'not with us right now'. The reason was not clear from the transcript.

signals.claim: Coker will be limited early in the week, ramp up Thursday, be cleared Friday and play Sunday vs. Atlanta.
signals.note: He is trending toward playing, but he was limited Wednesday, so Thursday and Friday practice participation is the thing to check.
signals.quote: So I expect him to play on Sunday.

signals.claim: Coker remains a featured part of the Panthers' offense.
signals.note: Canales praised his toughness and contested-catch ability, which supports his place in the passing game if healthy.
signals.quote: that's why he's become a part of what we're trying to feature

signals.claim: Metchie will take on a larger WR role and could see more snaps, especially if Coker is limited, and will handle some return duties.
signals.note: He is a depth WR who gains opportunity and could be a fill-in if Coker is limited or misses time.
signals.quote: this is an opportunity for John Metchie to step up in a role

signals.claim: Horn was waived for roster reasons, and Carolina hopes to bring him back on the practice squad.
signals.note: He has no fantasy relevance now, and his departure opens return and WR depth work for others.
signals.quote: the roster spot drove it

signals.claim: McMillan will continue to be the featured pass-game target and be moved around to create matchups.
signals.note: The coach confirmed he is the focal point of the passing offense, which supports his target volume even if defenses roll coverage his way.
signals.quote: There's no secret our offense in the pass game runs through Tmac

signals.claim: Legette is part of the game plan and will get chances in favorable matchups against Atlanta.
signals.note: Canales publicly backed him after a strong practice and said he expects good matchups, which makes him a possible bounce-back or deep-league option.
signals.quote: We're counting on XL.

signals.claim: Young is expected to build on a strong Week 1 performance.
signals.note: Canales called last week's game phenomenal and wants another step forward, which is a positive sign for the passing offense.
signals.quote: I just want to see him build off of last week.

signals.claim: Etienne is Carolina's preferred returner but is unavailable at the moment.
signals.note: His status is unclear, so the RB depth chart and return duties could shift.
signals.quote: Trevor's our guy. Unfortunately, he's not with us right now.

topics.detail: Carolina is preparing for Kevin Stefanski's system regardless of who starts at QB (Tua Tagovailoa, Michael Penix or Cooper Rush). Canales noted none are dynamic runners, so there's no zone-read element.
Canales respects Jeff Ulbrich's defense for its penetrating front, pressure packages and disguises. The secondary includes ball hawks such as Jessie Bates.
Atlanta's RB had about 30 touches last week. Carolina must always know where he is and tackle as a team, since he can bounce runs outside and attack vertically.
Canales praised the kickoff coverage and return units and the tight ends' contributions on special teams. He wants returners to get more yards beyond what is blocked.

title: Ben Johnson excited to be back at Soldier Field in front of Bears fans | Press Conference
headline: Bears prep for Minnesota (Flores' blitz-heavy defense) at home; Caleb Williams is playing with more anticipation, and Johnson says the ball will go to whoever is most consistent, naming Luther Burden III.
summary: Johnson previewed a hot Minnesota team (six straight wins) that runs the ball well, has skilled perimeter players like Jefferson, and has an uncertain quarterback situation. He praised Brian Flores' defense for blitzing from everywhere, including a lot of zero looks, and for forcing fumbles. Johnson said Chicago had a fumble last week that must be cleaned up. He acknowledged leaning right in the run game with Jonah Jackson and Darnell Wright, but said it is matchup-driven and he wants to complement it to the left. He singled out Minnesota DL Jonathan Redmond as an underrated force. Caleb Williams drew heavy praise for anticipation, confidence, and getting the offense into the right plays amid shifts, motions, and cadences. Johnson said the staff is committed to getting the ball to whichever runners, tight ends, and receivers execute most consistently, and he credited Luther Burden III in film-room highlights. He was critical of the defense, saying it lacked enough winning performances for championship-level play, and stressed the importance of the home crowd.

signals.claim: Williams will keep running the offense with pre-snap command and faster decisions against Minnesota's pressure looks.
signals.note: Coach confidence in Williams' processing and operation is a positive for the Bears passing game, though Flores' blitzes add risk.
signals.quote: he played with a lot of confidence... the game slows down to a degree.

signals.claim: Burden is among the receivers earning targets through consistent execution, and the offense will feed those doing it right.
signals.note: He was highlighted in the team film session alongside Williams, suggesting a growing role in the passing game.

signals.claim: Chicago may lean on the right-side run game with Jackson and Wright in some matchup-driven situations.
signals.note: Runs to the right behind Jackson and Wright could help Chicago's RBs, though Johnson said the volume varies weekly.

signals.claim: Wright will be a focal point of right-side runs, though Johnson said usage is matchup-driven.
signals.note: Strong right-side blocking is a positive environment for the Bears' backs.
signals.quote: we run it. Right. But we like to complement that as much to the left

topics.detail: Minnesota has won six straight, runs the ball at the second-highest rate over that stretch, and has dangerous perimeter weapons like Jefferson. The quarterback is unsettled, but Johnson still called it a darn good offense.

Flores blitzes from everywhere, brings zero more than any coordinator, and keeps opponents guessing. Johnson expects something new on tape and said Chicago must be detailed, sound, and win with a hat for a hat.
Johnson saw some three-and-outs and good technique but too few winning performances for championship-level defense. They need to respond after last week.
Chicago had a fumble last week that Johnson said needs to be cleaned up, especially against Minnesota's strip-heavy defense.
Johnson said the team needs the Soldier Field crowd and needs home wins to reach its season goals.

title: Zac Taylor Previews Week 2 Against Texans | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Zac Taylor owns Ja'Marr Chase's light Week 1 usage and says he must get him more touches at Houston, while Mike Gesicki is described as a matchup weapon who has found his groove.
summary: Taylor framed Week 2 at Houston as a tough road test against a fast, physical, veteran defense with elite talent, naming Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter, Denico Clowney and nickel Jalen Pitre. He took responsibility for Chase's quiet Week 1, saying the first-half script (a three-and-out, then short-field red zone drives) and the game flow limited his targets. He said it was no excuse and that, as the play caller, he has to find more ways to get Chase the ball. He rejected the idea that Chase is a decoy, though he admitted he is sometimes window dressing in the run game and that coverage shaded toward him opens one-on-ones for others. Taylor praised the tight end Mike (Gesicki) as a big, rangy receiver who beats man coverage, reads zones well and creates mismatches against nickels, safeties and linebackers. He compared Gesicki's chemistry with Burrow to Kelsey's and said he has hit the ground running this season. On the run game, Taylor said the backs ran well and the offense left some meat on the bone. He defended Joe Burrow's willingness to run for a first down and said he won't second-guess those decisions. He also praised the kicker's two 55+ yard field goals, which decided a six-point win, and called Houston QB C.J. Stroud poised, accurate and mobile.

signals.claim: Chase will be more heavily involved and get more touches in the Week 2 game plan at Houston than he did in Week 1.
signals.note: Taylor publicly blamed his own play calling for Chase's light Week 1 and said he is always a big part of the plan, which points to a target bounce-back.
signals.quote: I've got to continue to find ways

signals.claim: Gesicki will keep a featured pass-catching role, using his size to create mismatches against nickels, safeties and linebackers.
signals.note: Taylor described his chemistry with Burrow as near-automatic, which supports a steady target share as a TE option.
signals.quote: I think he's really found his groove.

signals.claim: Burrow will keep using his legs, such as scrambles and quarterback draws, when the situation calls for it.
signals.note: His rushing is a small fantasy bonus, but it carries some hit risk. Taylor said he isn't discouraging it.
signals.quote: I'm not going to second guess every decision he makes.

topics.detail: Houston returns most of its starters and has elite talent, speed and physicality at every level. Taylor singled out Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter, Denico Clowney and Jalen Pitre. He said they lost a safety last week and replaced him.
Taylor called Stroud poised, accurate and efficient, and said he can extend plays with his feet. He doesn't think the game from a couple of years ago applies much now.
Against a strong Tampa front, the backs ran well and Taylor felt the offense left yards on the field. He saw it as encouraging for a Week 1 performance.
The kicker was named player of the week for two field goals over 55 yards in a six-point win. Taylor credited the long snapper and holder, and the protection.
Taylor expects a loud, difficult atmosphere in Houston and said the win will take all three phases, including field position and the turnover battle.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 16th, 2026
headline: Dylan Sampson is headed to IR, opening RB touches for Raheim Sanders and practice-squad back Jay Mack, while Deshaun Watson keeps the starting job despite a rough Week 1 and rookie Austin Barber has locked down the starting tackle spot.
summary: Monken used the session to own a poor Week 1 loss to Jacksonville, saying the team was not good enough in coaching or play, and pointing to procedural penalties and cadence issues as part of the problem but not the whole cause. He said the offense went three-and-out repeatedly, which kept the defense on the field and prevented adjustments, and he did not regret deferring to take the ball first. He confirmed rookie tackle Austin Barber played well enough to stay the starter even when Tevin is healthy. He said the QB needs to be more consistent with his drops, and that Sampson's move to IR will open opportunities for Raheim Sanders and Jay Mack. On Deshaun Watson, he said he expects him to play well but did not frame Tampa as a must-win to keep the job, and he noted Watson had gone 22 months without playing and only recently got first-team reps. He defended his defensive approach, saying the team played a good amount of man, and that he hopes to see a big step up from everyone, Jared Verse included. He also spoke warmly of Baker Mayfield, praising his intelligence and competitiveness ahead of facing Tampa Bay.

injuries.detail: Being placed on injured reserve, described as 'for a little bit'; Raheim Sanders and Jay Mack will see expanded opportunities.

signals.claim: Will receive expanded opportunities at running back with Sampson on IR.
signals.note: Sampson's absence creates a path to RB touches for Sanders, though Jay Mack will share the opening.
signals.quote: it's going to open up opportunities for him and for Jay Mack

signals.claim: Watson remains the starting QB, but his play needs to improve and the offense around him needs to be better.
signals.note: Monken backed Watson without tying the job to one game, but he has been out 22 months and the Week 1 offense struggled, so his job security is worth monitoring.
signals.quote: I expect him to play really well.

signals.claim: Barber will remain the starting offensive tackle even once Tevin returns healthy.
signals.note: The coach said Barber has improved each week, which helps stabilize the Browns' pass protection.
signals.quote: Austin did great. Austin has been progressively getting better every week.

signals.claim: Verse is expected to improve in his second game with the new team.
signals.note: Monken gave only a general expectation of improvement and offered no role or snap detail.
signals.quote: I hope we expect a big step up with all of us

topics.detail: Monken said the team did not coach or play well enough against Jacksonville, that the offense's quick three-and-outs stopped the defense from adjusting, and that the team will own the mistakes and fix them.

Procedural issues came from several parts of the process, including getting the call in, huddling, and handling motions and shifts. The staff has been stressing the problem and will keep doing so, aiming to be elite at cadence.
Monken said the Browns played a decent amount of man and that some zone calls include match principles. He said the team is still working out its identity.
Monken said the QB needs to be more consistent with deep drops out of shotgun, framing it as one of several areas of team-wide inconsistency.
Monken praised Mayfield's intelligence, preparation, and competitiveness, and said he wishes he had done a better job with him in 2019.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Our Fans Give Us a Huge Advantage | Press Conference
headline: Schottenheimer says no lineup changes after Week 1; Pickens' drops are no concern, Guyton and T.J. Bass praised, and new RB Tyler Goodson was added as change-of-pace/special-teams depth
summary: Schottenheimer spent most of the session on the defense's Week 1 communication breakdowns. He said they were addressed in a team meeting, blamed the lapses on calls not being received rather than any one position, and expects a big improvement, although the home crowd noise will pose a challenge. He said there are no promotions or demotions in the lineup this week. He confirmed that Hooker had surgery that went well and is now in rehab, and that Demo is starting to work with the trainer. He praised Caleb Downs' debut, citing the strip sack and good coverage and communication, and he also complimented Tyler Guyton, T.J. Bass, and the young defenders Barham, Lawrence, and Ezeiruaku. He brushed off George Pickens' drops, saying he doesn't worry about him. He said the team signed Tyler Goodson to rebuild the RB room after Malik's injury, citing his speed, change of pace, and special teams value. He also owned his bad first play call, said the offense didn't get enough possessions, and wished he could have gotten the ball to George and CeeDee more. The next opponent is the Commanders, and the staff expects a tough front with Kinlaw and Payne, along with Jayden Daniels and the linebackers Sonny Styles and Lu vu.

injuries.detail: Had surgery that went well; now beginning the rehab phase.
A reporter called him 'Demo' and the coach said he will start working with the trainer (Britt); the nature and timeline of the injury weren't given, and a reporter assumed Barham would replace him.

signals.claim: Downs will remain a key defensive playmaker after a strong debut.
signals.note: The coach praised his first game, including the strip sack and coverage, which makes him a strong IDP option.
signals.quote: Caleb Downs is a tremendous football player.

signals.claim: Pickens will bounce back from the drops and remains a priority target.
signals.note: The coach shrugged off the drops and wants to get the ball to Pickens and CeeDee more, which is a buy-low sign.
signals.quote: I don't say anything to George. George will be just fine.

signals.claim: The coach wants to get Lamb more touches, though he said the Week 1 offense lacked possessions.
signals.note: Lamb should see more volume if the offense gets more drives.
signals.quote: anytime I get a ball to George and CD, I'd like to do that.

signals.claim: Guyton continues to play well at tackle.
signals.note: Good pass protection and run blocking help the offense's ceiling.
signals.quote: Tyler's playing really, really well.

signals.claim: Bass will keep playing on the offensive line.
signals.note: A steady, calm performer who graded out well and was praised by the coach, which helps the run game.
signals.quote: I thought T.J. played well. You know, we're not surprised by that.

signals.claim: Goodson will serve as a change-of-pace RB who can be active because of his special teams value.
signals.note: He is a depth piece, not a clear fantasy starter, and will help rebuild a room that lost Malik.
signals.quote: number one's got some speed, some juice, some change of pace ability.

signals.claim: Barham will keep playing at linebacker (possibly replacing Overshown) after a subpar first game.
signals.note: He is a rookie with an uncertain role, which makes him an IDP watch.
signals.quote: Did he play his best football ever? Nope. Did not.

topics.detail: Calls were made but not received, which caused busts; the team focused on being decisive and loud and on using hand signals. The coach said it isn't just a linebacker issue and expects a big improvement, although crowd noise at home will be a factor.
There will be no promotions or demotions this week, and the team will use its usual packages.

The coach praised Jayden Daniels' quick release and processing speed. He also praised Sonny Styles and the Commanders' front of Kinlaw and Payne, and he sees Dan Quinn's fingerprints on the defense under Daronte Jones.
The Giants ran for six yards a carry on first down, limiting the pass rush, and Dallas didn't have the ball enough. The coach took the blame for a bad first play call.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'He's a pro's pro'
headline: Jonnu Smith gave the Packers' 13-personnel looks real juice in Week 1, while the run game lacked volume (about 20 rushes) and Aaron Banks is being ramped back up this week.
summary: LaFleur praised Jonnu Smith as a 'pro's pro' who still has juice in his legs and can be moved around, noting explosive plays from 13 personnel in both the pass and run game, including a big completion on a keeper. He said the running backs (Brooks and Lloyd) didn't get many opportunities, roughly 20 rushes, and that staying ahead of the sticks is needed to get more. He admitted it would have been nice to lean on the run later in the game and that a running game opens up the passing game. Aaron Banks will be back at practice and the team is ramping him up over the week. LaFleur expects the shuffled offensive line to respond well to the tape and said the group has enough individual exposure to play well collectively. He called Christian Watson a player he doesn't worry about, with a great attitude, and said his strong play is no surprise. He said Jordan Love is consistent and ready to get back to work after taking the hits (the 15-18 pressure/sack count was referenced by a reporter). He previewed a physical, aggressive opponent defense under Brian Flores, praised a talented backfield duo (Paul and Braylon Allen) and a very good offensive line, and noted Edgerrin Cooper's versatility as a challenge for opposing offenses.

injuries.detail: Will be back out at practice this week; the team is ramping him up in a process that will take through the week.

signals.claim: Will continue to be moved around and used in 13 personnel for explosive plays in both the pass and run game.
signals.note: Smith's versatile role in multi-TE sets and strong praise point to continued usage, though it may cap Tucker Kraft's target share if the two share the field.
signals.quote: he's a pro's pro like the guy.

signals.claim: Running backs need more opportunities, which depends on staying ahead of the sticks and moving the chains.
signals.note: Backfield volume was limited (about 20 rushes), so RB opportunity depends on game script and offensive efficiency.

signals.claim: Running backs need more opportunities, which depends on staying ahead of the sticks and moving the chains.
signals.note: Limited rushing volume caps the fantasy ceiling for this backfield until the offense stays ahead of the sticks.

signals.claim: Banks will practice this week as the team works to ramp him up through the week.
signals.note: His return would help stabilize an offensive line that was shuffled by injuries and struggled, which affects the run game and Love's protection.
signals.quote: we're trying to get him ramped up ready to go.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase & Bengals Week 2 | Full Q&A

headline: Coen expects Travis Hunter's role to grow as he works back from injury, with the offense seeking more balance and a run game that struggled against Denver last year; Trevor Lawrence's legs and ball security drew praise.

topics.detail: Tennessee gave up yards in the run game, and Saleh named edge-setting as a top priority. It applies to ends, corners, linebackers and the three-technique. He cited Breece Hall's runs outside the numbers and said corners will be taught techniques to set the edge against guards.
The defense had no sacks and one hit. Saleh said the Jets held the ball and gave only about three legitimate rush chances. He is not concerned, but the rushers must win their one-on-ones.

The offense needs to improve at identifying and communicating in the run game and at getting on the same page in the passing game. Saleh said the Jets' coverage kept everything in front of the offense.

Saleh called the Week 1 performance well below the standard and said he expected a much better second half. He wants incremental weekly improvement and no reactionary changes, and says the team must prove itself week after week.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/16/26
headline: Frankie Luvu and Chig Okonkwo sat out the first practice with uncertain weekend status. Antonio Williams is trending up, and McLaurin is not guaranteed 10 targets.
summary: Quinn opened with injury news. Jordan McGee goes to IR and starts his return-to-play process, Theo is back at practice, and Frankie (Luvu) and Chig (Okonkwo) are out today with uncertainty heading into the weekend. He promised more clarity by Friday. He wants the team to 'level up' after Week 1, and said the secondary mistakes are correctable. He praised rookie WR Antonio Williams for his feel, composure and growth, including the low third-down catch against the Eagles. On Terry McLaurin's four targets, he said volume depends on how the game unfolds, so some weeks will be above 10 and others below. He said Luke McCaffrey and Treylon Burks were inactive in Week 1 because of the game plan and could be active in other weeks. He liked the RB's burst and cutback ability but stressed ball security after the fumble, and said Kaytron Allen's entry afterward was both planned and a response to it. Dorance Armstrong Jr. is back from injury and a welcome boost to the pass rush, while Trey Amos has no firm return timeline. The next opponent is Dallas, and Quinn is most worried about explosive plays from its receivers.

Quick feet suit the zone run game, though he has wins and losses in pass protection. Quinn likes where he is headed and expects more live reps to help.
Tyler Owens is a standout gunner and kick coverage player with some nickel and spy snaps. Quinn said he won't force more defensive work and will let roles be earned.
